text:
B: Alright, mate? Callum.
A: Alright. Darren.
B: You're the Castleford one, yeah? Danuta said. And Bethany. Everyone's been talking about you.
A: Have they now. Good things, I hope.
B: Mostly your socks, mate.
A: Oh, for God's sake. That's me finished, that. Where are you, then?
B: Plymouth. Student, second year, business and management. Work at a pub on the Barbican as well.
A: Business. Right. What you going to do with that?
B: Erm, sales, maybe. Or start something. Recruitment, estate agency, something with commission.
A: Commission. Yeah. Lot of lads think that. What do you do at the pub?
B: Glass collecting, pot washing. Bit of chatting to regulars. That's the main skill, really.
A: I'll bet it is. I'm a joiner, housing association. I get young lads come on jobs with us sometimes. Half of them stood on their phones while I'm on me knees doing the work.
B: Ha, I'd be that lad, to be fair. I'm honest.
A: At least you admit it. That's more than most.
B: My grandad worked at the dockyard, though. Proper hands-on. My mum says I've got none of it. I can't put a shelf up.
A: It's not hard, shelves. It's patience, mostly. And a spirit level. You'd be surprised how many people skip the spirit level.
B: I'd skip the spirit level.
A: Course you would. Do you watch any sport? Or is it all computer games?
B: Both. Argyle. Five-a-side Wednesdays. I'm a nightmare, I'll argue every foul.
A: Ha. I were the same at your age. Played league till I did me shoulder. I'm Cas Tigers. Lost again Sunday.
B: Bad ref?
A: Disgrace. Absolute disgrace. Sorry, I'm just being a grump.
B: Nah, you're alright, mate. Argyle lost too. Proper painful. We might go down, honestly.
A: Well. We're in it together, then.
B: Danuta told me to go to Krakow, by the way. Said it's cheap and the pierogi are proper.
A: She told me about pierogi an' all. And Lauren reckons I've got to book Krakow from East Midlands. I said I'd look tonight.
B: Mate, we should do it. Stag-do style. Nah, I'm joking.
A: Ha. I'd last one night. I'd be in bed by ten with a brew.
B: That's fine, you can mind the passports. You look like the organised one.
A: You've clearly not seen me van. Lost tenants' keys down the seat more than once.
B: Oh, so you're just like me, then, but with tools.
A: Don't push it, pal. Mind you, you might be right. Me sister'd say—
